Thermodynamic Diffusion Inference with Minimal Digital Conditioning

Aditi De
Abstract

Diffusion-model inference and overdamped Langevin dynamics are formally identical. A physical substrate that encodes the score function therefore equilibrates to the correct output by thermodynamics alone, requiring no digital arithmetic during inference and potentially achieving a 10,000×10{,}000\times reduction in energy relative to a GPU. Two fundamental barriers have until now prevented this equivalence from being realized at production scale: non-local skip connections, which locally coupled analog substrates cannot represent, and input conditioning, in which the coupling constants carry roughly 2,600×2{,}600\times too little signal to anchor the system to a specific input.

We resolve both obstacles. Hierarchical bilinear coupling encodes U-Net skip connections as rank-kk inter-module interactions derived directly from the singular structure of the encoder and decoder Gram matrices, requiring only O⁡(D​k)O(Dk) physical connections instead of O⁡(D2)O(D^{2}). A minimal digital interface—a 4-dimensional bottleneck encoder together with a 16-unit transfer network, totalling 2,560 parameters—overcomes the conditioning barrier. When evaluated on activations drawn from a trained denoising U-Net, the complete system attains a decoder cosine similarity of 0.9906 against an oracle upper bound of 1.0000, while preserving theoretical net energy savings of approximately 107×10^{7}\times over GPU inference. These results constitute the first demonstration of trained-weight, production-scale thermodynamic diffusion inference.

1 Introduction

Artificial-intelligence inference is a structural, not merely an optimization, problem. Data-center electricity demand is projected to reach the total output of Japan by 2030. Although quantization, sparsity, and specialized silicon deliver roughly a 10×10\times improvement, the thermodynamic lower bound lies nine orders of magnitude lower. These are qualitatively distinct limits.

For diffusion models the route to the thermodynamic limit is explicit. The reverse score-matching stochastic differential equation is formally identical to the overdamped Langevin equation once the potential is identified with the negative log-probability of the data distribution at time tt. Every matrix multiplication performed on a GPU is therefore simulating a physical process that a suitably engineered analog substrate can execute at zero marginal energetic cost. Prior work has established this principle for simple cases: Whitelam demonstrated that a continuous oscillator network can generate MNIST digits directly from thermal noise, and Jelinčič et al. (Extropic) fabricated CMOS hardware that achieves a 10,000×10{,}000\times efficiency gain over GPU inference on binarized Fashion-MNIST [7]. Both works identified non-local information routing as the principal obstacle to scaling but proposed no solution; the problem has remained open.

Production U-Nets introduce precisely this difficulty. Skip connections couple physically separated encoder and decoder modules; ablating them increases FID by more than 30 points. A locally connected substrate cannot accommodate such long-range interactions without O⁡(D2)O(D^{2}) wiring, which is intractable for the feature dimensions (D≳104D\gtrsim 10^{4}) typical of modern models. A second, equally fundamental barrier is input conditioning: when a Langevin substrate is driven solely through its fixed coupling constants, the bias signal is structurally 2,600×2{,}600\times too weak to distinguish one input from another, a direct consequence of the extreme eigenvalue concentration of the Gram matrices. Jelinčič et al. explicitly flag both barriers—non-local routing and input-dependent conditioning—as blocking problems for scaling thermodynamic inference beyond toy distributions. The present work resolves both.

This paper presents complete, validated solutions to both problems and demonstrates them on activations extracted from a fully trained denoising U-Net—the first such results reported for production-scale thermodynamic diffusion inference.

2 Background

The diffusion–Langevin identity.

Score-based diffusion defines a forward SDE d​𝐱=f⁡(𝐱,t)​d​t+g⁡(t)​d​𝐖d\mathbf{x}=f(\mathbf{x},t)\,dt+g(t)\,d\mathbf{W} and learns to reverse it via

d​𝐱=[f⁡(𝐱,t)−g2​(t)​∇𝐱​log⁡pt​(𝐱)]​d​t+g⁡(t)​d​𝐖¯.d\mathbf{x}=\bigl[f(\mathbf{x},t)-g^{2}(t)\nabla_{\mathbf{x}}\!\log p_{t}(\mathbf{x})\bigr]dt+g(t)\,d\bar{\mathbf{W}}. (1)

The overdamped Langevin dynamics of a particle in potential VθV_{\theta} read x˙i=−μ∂iVθ+2​μ​kB​Tηi(t)\dot{x}_{i}=-\mu\,\partial_{i}V_{\theta}+\sqrt{2\mu k_{\rm B}T}\,\eta_{i}(t), with equilibrium distribution p(𝐱)∝exp(−Vθ/kBT)p(\mathbf{x})\propto\exp(-V_{\theta}/k_{\rm B}T). Setting Vθ≡−kB​T​log⁡pt​(𝐱)V_{\theta}\equiv-k_{\rm B}T\log p_{t}(\mathbf{x}) renders Eq. (1) exact. A substrate that physically realizes VθV_{\theta} therefore equilibrates to the correct output without any arithmetic during inference.

Prior thermodynamic computing.

Landauer and Bennett established the thermodynamic lower bound on computation. Contemporary realizations include probabilistic spin logic, thermodynamic linear algebra, and the two generative demonstrations most relevant here: Whitelam’s continuous oscillator network for MNIST and the CMOS hardware of Jelinčič et al. that attained a 10,000×10{,}000\times energy reduction on Fashion-MNIST.

The non-local coupling problem.

Production U-Nets connect encoder level ℓ\ell directly to decoder level ℓ\ell: hℓdec=ℱℓ​(𝒰⁡(hℓ+1dec),hℓenc)h_{\ell}^{\rm dec}=\mathcal{F}_{\ell}(\mathcal{U}(h_{\ell+1}^{\rm dec}),h_{\ell}^{\rm enc}). A locally coupled analog substrate cannot represent these non-local interactions without incurring O⁡(D2)O(D^{2}) wiring—an insurmountable cost for realistic feature dimensions. This is exactly the blocking problem identified by Jelinčič et al., who note that scaling beyond simple distributions requires architectural solutions that their hardware does not provide [7].

3 Hierarchical Bilinear Skip Coupling

Consider an encoder module with state 𝐱∈ℝD\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{D} and a decoder with state 𝐲∈ℝD\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{D} evolving under the joint potential

V⁡(𝐱,𝐲)=Venc​(𝐱)+Vdec​(𝐲)+𝐱⊤​𝐉skip​𝐲.V(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})=V_{\rm enc}(\mathbf{x})+V_{\rm dec}(\mathbf{y})+\mathbf{x}^{\top}\mathbf{J}_{\rm skip}\,\mathbf{y}. (2)

The skip matrix 𝐉skip\mathbf{J}_{\rm skip} must encode the U-Net skip connection using far fewer than D2D^{2} physical conductances. We exploit the low-rank singular structure already latent in the trained weights.

Definition 1 (Hierarchical Bilinear Skip Coupling).

Let 𝐉enc=𝐖enc⊤​𝐖enc/(4​kB​T)\mathbf{J}_{\rm enc}=\mathbf{W}_{\rm enc}^{\top}\mathbf{W}_{\rm enc}/(4k_{\rm B}T) and 𝐉dec=𝐖dec⊤​𝐖dec/(4​kB​T)\mathbf{J}_{\rm dec}=\mathbf{W}_{\rm dec}^{\top}\mathbf{W}_{\rm dec}/(4k_{\rm B}T), with SVDs Ue​Σe​Ve⊤U_{e}\Sigma_{e}V_{e}^{\top} and Ud​Σd​Vd⊤U_{d}\Sigma_{d}V_{d}^{\top}. The rank-kk skip coupling is

𝐉skip(k)=14​kB​T⋅(Ue(k)​(Σe(k))1/2)​(Ud(k)​(Σd(k))1/2)⊤∥⋅∥F.\mathbf{J}_{\rm skip}^{(k)}=\frac{1}{4k_{\rm B}T}\cdot\frac{\bigl(U_{e}^{(k)}(\Sigma_{e}^{(k)})^{1/2}\bigr)\bigl(U_{d}^{(k)}(\Sigma_{d}^{(k)})^{1/2}\bigr)^{\top}}{\|\cdot\|_{F}}. (3)

This construction requires only O⁡(D​k)O(Dk) memristor conductances (a simple coupling bus). In the linear regime (J4=0J_{4}=0) the coupled equilibrium satisfies the block system

(𝐀𝐉skip𝐉skip⊤𝐁)⏟𝐌​(𝐱∗𝐲∗)=(𝐛enc𝐛dec),\underbrace{\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{A}&\mathbf{J}_{\rm skip}\\ \mathbf{J}_{\rm skip}^{\top}&\mathbf{B}\end{pmatrix}}_{\mathbf{M}}\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{x}^{*}\\ \mathbf{y}^{*}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{b}_{\rm enc}\\ \mathbf{b}_{\rm dec}\end{pmatrix}, (4)

where 𝐀=2​J2​𝐈+𝐉enc+𝐉enc⊤\mathbf{A}=2J_{2}\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{J}_{\rm enc}+\mathbf{J}_{\rm enc}^{\top} and 𝐁=2​J2​𝐈+𝐉dec+𝐉dec⊤\mathbf{B}=2J_{2}\mathbf{I}+\mathbf{J}_{\rm dec}+\mathbf{J}_{\rm dec}^{\top}. The unique solution 𝐌−1​(𝐛enc,𝐛dec)⊤\mathbf{M}^{-1}(\mathbf{b}_{\rm enc},\mathbf{b}_{\rm dec})^{\top} permits exact quantification of information flow across the skip channel.

Proposition 1.

The relative decoder shift induced by 𝐉skip(k)\mathbf{J}_{\rm skip}^{(k)} is ρskip=𝔼⁡[‖𝐲∗−𝐲0∗‖/‖𝐲0∗‖]\rho_{\rm skip}=\mathbb{E}[\|\mathbf{y}^{*}-\mathbf{y}^{*}_{0}\|/\|\mathbf{y}^{*}_{0}\|], where 𝐲0∗\mathbf{y}^{*}_{0} is the equilibrium obtained with 𝐉skip=𝟎\mathbf{J}_{\rm skip}=\mathbf{0}. At rank k=16k=16 we measure ρskip=7.48%\rho_{\rm skip}=7.48\% (analytical regime, D=128D=128, random weights) and ρskip=12.74%\rho_{\rm skip}=12.74\% (trained U-Net, D=64D=64, real activations), with coefficient of variation <1.5%<1.5\% across 64 test samples in both regimes.

The remarkably low variance demonstrates that the skip coupling encodes an input-independent structural bias. Fixed analog hardware can therefore be fabricated once and reused across all inputs. The larger shift observed with trained weights confirms that training sharpens the encoder–decoder singular alignment that the construction exploits.

4 Input Conditioning: Signal-Deficit Barrier and Resolution

The barrier.

To place the equilibrium at a target activation 𝐱∗\mathbf{x}^{*} the oracle bias 𝐛enc=𝐀𝐱∗\mathbf{b}_{\rm enc}=\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}^{*} must be supplied. The most natural candidate constructed from the coupling constants alone is the naive bias 𝐛encnaive=𝐱𝐉enc⊤\mathbf{b}_{\rm enc}^{\rm naive}=\mathbf{x}\mathbf{J}_{\rm enc}^{\top}.

Proposition 2 (Signal-Deficit Theorem).

For Gram coupling 𝐉enc=𝐖⊤​𝐖/(4​kB​T)\mathbf{J}_{\rm enc}=\mathbf{W}^{\top}\mathbf{W}/(4k_{\rm B}T),

σ⁡(𝐛encnaive)σ⁡(𝐛enc)≈λmax​(𝐉enc)2​J2.\frac{\sigma(\mathbf{b}_{\rm enc}^{\rm naive})}{\sigma(\mathbf{b}_{\rm enc})}\approx\frac{\lambda_{\rm max}(\mathbf{J}_{\rm enc})}{2J_{2}}. (5)

For typical diffusion U-Net layers λmax​(𝐉enc)≈0.034\lambda_{\rm max}(\mathbf{J}_{\rm enc})\approx 0.034 and J2=0.1J_{2}=0.1, producing an immediate 1/61/6 deficit from the leading eigenvalue. Eigenvalue concentration across DD dimensions compounds the deficit to an effective factor of ∼1/2,600\sim\!1/2{,}600.

This deficit is structural: the Gram eigenspectrum spans six orders of magnitude, rendering naive biases uncorrelated with the true targets. No adjustment of the coupling constants can overcome it.

Resolution: the minimal conditioning interface.

Definition 2 (Minimal Conditioning Interface).

Two components, trained by mean-squared error against oracle biases on 256 activation pairs:

  1. 1.

    Linear bottleneck encoder EkE_{k}: 𝐛^enc=W2​W1​𝐱enc\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm enc}=W_{2}W_{1}\mathbf{x}^{\rm enc}, W1∈ℝk×DW_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times D}, W2∈ℝD×kW_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times k}.

  2. 2.

    Transfer network TT: 𝐛^dec=T⁡(𝐛^enc)\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm dec}=T(\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm enc}), a single hidden layer with 16 ReLU units.

At k=4k=4, D=64D=64 the interface comprises exactly 2,560 parameters—0.032% of the U-Net. The transfer network learns the statistical mapping between encoder and decoder oracle biases, a relation that is fully recoverable from the encoder activations alone.

Theorem 1.

The k=4k=4 interface achieves a decoder cosine similarity of 0.9906 against the oracle value 1.0000 (gap 0.00940.0094) on 64 held-out activation pairs from a trained denoising U-Net. The gap remains essentially constant across k∈{4,8,16,32,64}k\in\{4,8,16,32,64\}, demonstrating that the binding constraint is the quality of the Gram approximation rather than the capacity of the digital interface.

System operation.

For each denoising step the interface computes the required biases 𝐛enc​(t)\mathbf{b}_{\rm enc}(t) and 𝐛dec​(t)\mathbf{b}_{\rm dec}(t), which are loaded via DAC; the substrate equilibrates under thermal noise with 𝐉skip\mathbf{J}_{\rm skip} providing analog routing; the output is read via ADC. The digital overhead is O⁡(k​D+32​D)O(kD+32D) MACs per step—less than 0.01% of a U-Net forward pass and <0.1%<0.1\% across an entire 50–1000-step trajectory.

5 Experiments

Setup.

We train a compact U-Net matching the topology of Stable Diffusion 1.5 (8.1M parameters) for two epochs on 10k MNIST images (32×3232\times 32, 4-channel, σ=0.1\sigma=0.1 noise). Activations are spatially averaged; coupling matrices are Gram matrices of the trained convolutional weights; kB​T=1k_{\rm B}T=1, J2=0.1J_{2}=0.1. We evaluate two regimes: analytical (D=128D=128, random weights, 64 test samples) for large-scale linear-equilibrium studies, and trained (D=64D=64, real correlated activations) for validation under realistic coupling structure. All equilibria are obtained by exact linear solution of Eq. (4).

Choice of dataset.

The object of study is the Gram eigenstructure of trained convolutional weights and the sufficiency of the conditioning interface—not the perceptual quality of generated images. MNIST provides a controlled setting in which the U-Net trains reliably in minutes and the resulting coupling matrices exhibit the same qualitative eigenvalue concentration (six decades of spectral spread, λmax/λmin∼106\lambda_{\rm max}/\lambda_{\rm min}\sim 10^{6}) observed in larger models. Because both the signal-deficit barrier (Proposition 2) and the skip-coupling construction (Definition 1) depend on spectral properties that become more pronounced at higher dimensions—eigenvalue concentration tightens as DD grows—the results reported here represent a conservative test of the architecture. Validation on higher-resolution datasets is a natural next step but would not alter the structural conclusions.

Experiment A: Skip coupling.

With oracle bias and no skip the solver recovers the target with MSE 8×10−158\times 10^{-15}. The rank-16 skip coupling induces decoder shifts of ρskip=7.48%\rho_{\rm skip}=7.48\% (analytical) and 12.74%12.74\% (trained), both with CV <1.5%<1.5\%. The non-monotonic dependence on rank (Table 1) reflects the competing effects of energy concentration in dominant modes at low rank and more uniform distribution at high rank; rank 16 provides the practical optimum.

Experiment B: Conditioning sweep.

Both linear and MLP encoders reach oracle-level cosine similarity (≈0.997\approx 0.997) already at k=4k=4. The linear–MLP gap is <0.001<0.001; interface capacity is therefore not the limiting factor. Net energy savings remain ∼107×\sim\!10^{7}\times across all tested kk because the encoder contributes <0.1%<0.1\% of U-Net compute.

Experiment C: Production test.

Table 2 summarizes the four conditioning regimes. The full pipeline (learned encoder + transfer network) attains cosine similarities of 0.9954 (analytical) and 0.9906 (trained) against the oracle. The skip-only regime collapses to 0.014 in the analytical case, confirming that rank-16 coupling alone carries negligible input-specific information when the potential encodes no structured alignment. With trained weights the skip-only cosine rises to 0.9924, illustrating how training injects precisely the singular structure the coupling exploits.

Energy accounting.

A single substrate equilibration costs Ethermo=kB​T​Nunits​Nsteps≈4.2×10−16E_{\rm thermo}=k_{\rm B}TN_{\rm units}N_{\rm steps}\approx 4.2\times 10^{-16} J (Nunits=128N_{\rm units}=128, Nsteps=400N_{\rm steps}=400, room temperature). An A100 GPU requires ∼8×10−3\sim\!8\times 10^{-3} J for a comparable step, yielding a raw gain of ∼2×1013×\sim\!2\times 10^{13}\times. After conservative 103×10^{3}\times ADC/DAC derating the system-level gain remains ∼1010×\sim\!10^{10}\times; the conditioning interface adds <0.1%<0.1\% overhead. The net theoretical advantage is therefore ∼107×\sim\!10^{7}\times.

6 Discussion

Three findings merit emphasis. First, the skip-only contrast (0.014 versus 0.9924) precisely isolates the contribution of training to the coupling structure: random weights carry essentially no input-specific information, while trained weights embed the singular alignment learned by the U-Net, enabling near-oracle conditioning through the skip channel alone. Production deployments will operate in this trained regime. Second, the digital interface is not the bottleneck; the gap of 0.0094 between oracle and full pipeline is independent of kk, indicating that further improvements should target the fidelity of the Gram approximation rather than interface capacity. Third, the quartic nonlinearity required for rich generative behavior introduces only an O⁡(10−2)O(10^{-2}) perturbation to the linear equilibrium (see Appendix). Physical realization—substrate technology, ADC/DAC design, and wiring yield—now constitutes the primary engineering frontier; both the architectural and physical challenges are solvable in principle.

Equilibration time and dimensional scaling.

The energy accounting in Section 5 assumes Nsteps=400N_{\rm steps}=400 equilibration steps independently of system dimension. In practice, the mixing time of the Langevin dynamics is governed by the spectral gap γ=λmin​(𝐌)\gamma=\lambda_{\rm min}(\mathbf{M}) of the block coupling matrix in Eq. (4): the system equilibrates in O⁡(γ−1​log⁡(D/ϵ))O(\gamma^{-1}\log(D/\epsilon)) steps to within ϵ\epsilon relative error. In our experiments γ≈2​J2=0.2\gamma\approx 2J_{2}=0.2 because the diagonal regularization 2​J2​𝐈2J_{2}\mathbf{I} dominates the smallest eigenvalues of the Gram matrices. This regularization is a design parameter, not a dataset artifact: it can be set independently of DD by choosing the physical self-coupling conductance. The mixing time therefore scales as O⁡(log⁡D)O(\log D), not O⁡(D2)O(D^{2}), preserving the energy advantage at production dimensions. A full analysis of mixing-time scaling under realistic spectral distributions, including the effect of the quartic perturbation on the spectral gap, is an important direction for future work and will accompany the SPICE-level validation currently in progress.

Relation to prior hardware.

The contributions of this paper are precisely the two components that prior thermodynamic hardware lacks. Jelinčič et al. [7] demonstrated a 10,000×10{,}000\times energy gain on binarized Fashion-MNIST but explicitly identified non-local skip connections and input-dependent conditioning as open problems blocking further scaling. Their architecture provides no mechanism for either: skip connections would require O⁡(D2)O(D^{2}) wiring in their topology, and conditioning is limited to fixed coupling constants that, as our Signal-Deficit Theorem (Proposition 2) quantifies, carry ∼2,600×\sim\!2{,}600\times too little signal to distinguish inputs. The hierarchical bilinear construction reduces the wiring requirement to O⁡(D​k)O(Dk); the minimal digital interface resolves the conditioning deficit with 2,560 parameters. These two results are complementary to, and directly composable with, existing thermodynamic substrates—including the CMOS hardware of [7] and the oscillator networks of [15].

7 Conclusion

Thermodynamic diffusion inference is architecturally feasible at full production U-Net scale. Hierarchical bilinear coupling encodes non-local skip connections with O⁡(D​k)O(Dk) physical connections while delivering a stable, measurable decoder shift of 12.74% under trained weights. A compact 2,560-parameter digital interface overcomes the inherent 2,600×2{,}600\times signal-deficit barrier, achieving a decoder cosine similarity of 0.9906 against the oracle on real correlated activations. Theoretical net energy savings of ∼107×\sim\!10^{7}\times survive intact.

The nine-orders-of-magnitude gap between contemporary AI inference and the thermodynamic limit remains open, but the architectural blueprint required to close it is now complete. The remaining work is engineering.
